unmapped_findings: Table 4 (inference time per image) on LCS (1360 × 600, polycrystalline, ARI metric): Watershed 0.54 / 6.12 ms, OTSU 0.64 / 4.54 ms, Canny 0.73 / 16.48 ms, SAM 0.86 / 1850.35 ms, MatSAM 0.96 / 1926.35 ms (source: b0115, figure_unlabelled_005).

On the LCS dataset, MatSAM achieves an ARI score of 0.96 with an inference time of 1926.35 ms per image, compared to OTSU's 4.54 ms; the high accuracy comes at a higher computational cost (source: b0117).

LCS [11] is analyzed qualitatively in Fig. 6 because the public dataset does not provide released labels; MatSAM demonstrates comparable recognition performance to the original specialist method without human intervention (source: b0074, b0076).
The real-size field of view for LCS in Fig. 1 is blank ('------'); only the pixel resolution 1360 × 600 pix is given (source: figure_001).

LCS is grouped as 'boundary' type in Table 1 (together with SS, HEA, PI-2); for polycrystalline images, grain boundary masks were extracted from the segmented grain regions using a contour-finding approach (source: b0036, b0045).

MatSAM not only segments almost all grains in LCS but also accurately identifies the vast majority of incomplete and blurred grain boundaries; despite the large variation in image resolution within this dataset, MatSAM consistently outputs satisfactory results (source: b0066).

Processing/history of the LCS steel is not reported in this paper; it is a public dataset [11] whose original labels were not provided, and part of the raw images was annotated for evaluation (source: b0024).
